title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: Quarta ratio — ante judicium
pass_a_gloss: Fourth reason: punishment properly so called, or the death which the law was threatening, ought to have followed God's inquiry and judgment concerning the violation of that law. But privation of justice, or spiritual death, did not follow God's inquiry and judgment concerning the violation of the law, but preceded it: it was not therefore punishment properly so called, or the death which the law was threatening.
pass_b_english: Fourth proof. Proper punishment—the death the law named—has to come after God has examined and judged the breach. Loss of righteousness, spiritual death, did not wait for that examination and judgment; it arrived first. Therefore it was neither proper punishment nor the death the law was threatening.
source_text: Quarta ratio, poena proprie dicta sive mors quam lex comminabatur sequi debuit quaestionem ac judicium Dei de violatione illius legis. Sed privatio justitiae sive mors spiritualis quaestionem ac judicium Dei de violatione legis sequuta non est, sed antecessit: non fuit igitur poena proprie dicta, sive mors quam lex comminabatur.

choices.choice: poena must follow judicium; privatio preceded it
